questions.question: A university wants to display live captions while lecturers speak in classrooms. Which capability of Azure Speech in Foundry Tools should the university use?

options.why: Text to speech converts written text into audio. Captions require converting audio into text.
Correct. Real-time speech recognition transcribes speech as it is spoken, which is required for live captions.
Custom voice creates a unique synthetic voice and does not produce captions.
Batch transcription processes recorded files asynchronously and is not suitable for live captions.

questions.explanation: Live captions require real-time speech to text, which converts spoken audio into text as it is received.

questions.scenario: A bank records customer support calls. Compliance officers need transcripts that show which statements were made by the support agent and which were made by the customer.
questions.question: Which feature should the bank use?

options.why: Correct. Speaker diarization labels each segment of the transcript with the speaker who said it.
Speech translation converts speech into another language. It does not identify speakers.
SSML controls how synthesized speech sounds. It is not used for transcription.
Neural text to speech produces audio from text and does not analyze recordings.

questions.explanation: Speaker diarization separates a transcript by speaker, answering the question of who spoke when.

questions.question: A developer uses a neural voice to read one-time passwords aloud. Which TWO adjustments can the developer make by using Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML)?

options.text: Slow the speaking rate when the password digits are read
options.why: Correct. The prosody element in SSML controls speaking rate.

options.text: Insert a pause before the expiry message
options.why: Correct. The break element in SSML inserts a pause of a specified length.

options.text: Identify the language of incoming customer audio
options.why: Identifying the language of incoming audio is a speech recognition feature, not an SSML capability.

options.text: Label which caller spoke each sentence
options.why: Labeling speakers is speaker diarization, a speech-to-text feature.

questions.explanation: SSML controls how text is spoken, including rate, pitch, pauses, pronunciation and speaking style.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company finds that speech-to-text transcripts frequently misrecognize drug names used by its staff. A phrase list has not improved accuracy sufficiently. What should the company use?

options.why: Correct. Custom speech trains the recognition model with the company's own audio and text to improve accuracy for specialized vocabulary.
Custom voice changes how synthesized speech sounds. It does not improve recognition accuracy.
Temperature is a generative model parameter and does not affect speech recognition accuracy.
Speech translation converts speech to another language and does not improve recognition of specialized terms.

questions.explanation: Custom speech adapts the speech recognition model to specific vocabulary, accents and audio conditions.

questions.question: A travel app must listen to a traveler speaking Hindi and display the words in English text. Which capability should the app use?

options.why: Text to speech produces audio from text. The input here is speech.
Correct. Speech translation recognizes speech in one language and returns text or speech in another language.
Speaker diarization identifies speakers but does not translate.
Key phrase extraction finds talking points in text and does not process audio or translate.

questions.explanation: Speech translation combines recognition and translation so that spoken input in one language becomes output in another.
